hook.en: Twenty kinds of beads can make millions of different necklaces. Twenty amino acids make every protein in your body, from hair keratin to the haemoglobin in your blood.
hook.kn: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಬಗೆಯ ಮಣಿಗಳಿಂದ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ಬಗೆಯ ಹಾರಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡಬಹುದು. ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಅಮೈನೋ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ನಿಮ್ಮ ದೇಹದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Explain why lipids appear in the acid-insoluble fraction.
State the functions of proteins and name the most abundant ones.
Describe the four levels of protein structure.

narration.en: Twenty kinds of beads can make millions of different necklaces. Twenty amino acids make every protein in your body, from hair keratin to the haemoglobin in your blood.
narration.kn: ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಬಗೆಯ ಮಣಿಗಳಿಂದ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ಬಗೆಯ ಹಾರಗಳನ್ನು ಮಾಡಬಹುದು. ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತು ಅಮೈನೋ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳು ನಿಮ್ಮ ದೇಹದ ಎಲ್ಲ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ರೂಪಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Molecules in the acid-insoluble fraction, other than lipids, have molecular weights of ten thousand daltons and above; these are biomacromolecules: proteins, nucleic acids and polysaccharides. Lipids have molecular weights below 800 Da, yet they come in the acid-insoluble fraction because grinding breaks cell membranes into water-insoluble vesicles. The acid-soluble pool roughly represents the cytoplasmic composition; the macromolecules of the cytoplasm and organelles form the acid-insoluble fraction.

points.en: Proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides: true macromolecules.
Lipids: small, but appear in the insoluble fraction as membrane vesicles.
Water is the most abundant chemical in living organisms.

narration.kn: ಲಿಪಿಡ್ ಹೊರತುಪಡಿಸಿ ಆಮ್ಲ-ಅವಿಲೇಯ ಭಾಗದ ಅಣುಗಳು ಹತ್ತು ಸಾವಿರ ಡಾಲ್ಟನ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ತೂಕದ ಬೃಹದಣುಗಳು. ಲಿಪಿಡ್ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಅಣುವಾದರೂ ಪೊರೆಯ ಕೋಶಕಗಳಾಗಿ ಅವಿಲೇಯ ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Let us draw an amino acid, join two of them, and then build the four levels of protein structure.

say.en: Every amino acid has a central carbon carrying a hydrogen, an amino group, a carboxyl group and a variable R group.
Twenty kinds of R group give twenty amino acids: hydrogen in glycine, methyl in alanine, hydroxymethyl in serine.
The carboxyl of one amino acid joins the amino group of the next. A water molecule is removed and a peptide bond forms.
The primary structure is the sequence of amino acids, from the N-terminal to the C-terminal end.
The chain coils, most often into a right-handed alpha helix: that is the secondary structure.
The helix folds on itself like a ball of wool. This tertiary structure gives the 3-D shape needed for activity.
Several folded chains can join. Adult haemoglobin has four subunits, two alpha and two beta: the quaternary structure.

body.en: Proteins are polypeptides: linear chains of amino acids linked by peptide bonds, formed when the carboxyl group of one amino acid reacts with the amino group of the next with loss of water. Essential amino acids must come from food; non-essential ones are made by the body. Proteins transport nutrients across membranes, fight infections, act as hormones (insulin) and enzymes (trypsin), and give structure (collagen). Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world, and RuBisCO is the most abundant protein in the whole biosphere. Primary structure is the sequence of amino acids, written from the N-terminal (first) to the C-terminal (last) amino acid. Parts of the chain fold into a helix (only right-handed helices are observed) as secondary structure; the whole chain folds on itself like a hollow woollen ball as tertiary structure; and more than one polypeptide assemble as quaternary structure. Adult human haemoglobin has 4 subunits: 2 α and 2 β.

points.en: Peptide bond: between –COOH of one amino acid and –NH₂ of the next.
Tertiary structure gives the 3-D view needed for biological activity.

narration.kn: ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗಳು ಪೆಪ್ಟೈಡ್ ಬಂಧದಿಂದ ಜೋಡಿಸಿದ ಅಮೈನೋ ಆಮ್ಲಗಳ ಸರಪಳಿಗಳು. ಪ್ರಾಣಿ ಜಗತ್ತಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊಲಾಜೆನ್, ಜೀವಗೋಳದಲ್ಲಿ ರುಬಿಸ್ಕೊ ಅತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಇರುವ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್. ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ರಚನೆಗೆ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ, ದ್ವಿತೀಯಕ, ತೃತೀಯಕ ಮತ್ತು ಚತುರ್ಥಕ ಹಂತಗಳಿವೆ.

caption.en: Joining n amino acids needs n − 1 peptide bonds and releases n − 1 water molecules. With 20 kinds of amino acid, the number of possible sequences is 20 to the power n.

tryThis.en: How many peptide bonds hold a chain of 51 amino acids (insulin)?
Find n for a protein of about 11 000 Da.
Why can a few kinds of amino acid make so many proteins?

problem.en: A tripeptide is made from three amino acids. How many peptide bonds and how many water molecules are released in forming it? How many peptide bonds are there in a polypeptide of 100 amino acids?

steps.en: Each peptide bond joins two amino acids and releases one water molecule (dehydration).
A chain of n amino acids has n − 1 peptide bonds.
Tripeptide: 3 − 1 = 2 bonds and 2 water molecules; 100 amino acids: 99 bonds.

answer.en: 2 peptide bonds and 2 H₂O; 99 peptide bonds

body.en: In the animal world it is collagen, the protein of skin, tendons and bone. In the whole biosphere it is RuBisCO, the carbon-fixing enzyme in every green leaf.
